label: UniFi U7 In-Wall
description: UniFi U7 In-Wall (U7-IW) - 3x 2.5G RJ45. 802.3af PoE-in; WiFi 7; up to 4.3 Gbps PHY rate; 13 W max.
notes: PoE draw read 2026-11-28 from https://techspecs.ui.com/unifi/wifi/u7-iw (HTTP 200, 650,261 B): the specification table prints "Power Method: PoE / PoE+ (Required for PoE output)" and "Max. Power Consumption: 13W". 13 W is that figure and it sits on eth0, where the catalogue's other in-wall AP (u6-iw) also carries its input jack. Until this pass the port carried no poeIn at all, so engine/media.js fell back to its 12.95 W 802.3af class default and the model drew 12.95 W whatever the datasheet said. Nothing in the engine compares a PD's draw with the class its PSE declared, so cabling this AP to an 802.3af port is still accepted; the number changes the budget arithmetic, which is the one thing a PoE lab asks of it. The Built-In Switch row in the same table prints "(1) PoE+ input and (1) PoE output", so once fed 802.3at this box can pass power to a downstream device, and the 13 W is the vendor's own "13W (Excluding PoE output)". No port is marked poeOut here because the table names no index for either jack and the datasheet slug dl.ui.com/ds/u7-iw_ds.pdf answers 302: the only Ubiquiti surface that states the passthrough declines to say which of the three ports carries it, and an index guessed there cables the wrong jack.
